facts.raw_span: A 67-year-old man
hypertension, dyslipidaemia, stage 3 chronic kidney disease, active smoking (35 pack-years), a family history of ischaemic heart disease
prior percutaneous coronary interventions (2008, 2017, 2022) for non-ST-elevation myocardial infarction
Canadian Cardiovascular Society Class III angina
exercise stress test induced angina at 50 W without ECG changes
normal sinus rhythm, Q waves in lead III, and biphasic T waves in leads III and aVF
left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) of 65% without regional wall-motion abnormalities
patent stents in the circumflex artery, non-significant disease in the left anterior descending artery, and significant ostial right coronary artery stenosis
ST-segment elevation in leads V1–V3
subocclusion of the right coronary postero-lateral branch
recurrent sustained polymorphic ventricular tachycardia and ventricular fibrillation
new QTc prolongation to 500 ms

concepts.why: The patient has a history of non-ST-elevation myocardial infarction and presents with ST-segment elevation in leads V1–V3, indicating acute coronary syndrome.

The patient developed recurrent sustained polymorphic ventricular tachycardia and ventricular fibrillation, and echocardiography revealed akinesia of all apical segments, leading to suspicion of takotsubo syndrome.
The patient has a family history of ischaemic heart disease and presents with Canadian Cardiovascular Society Class III angina, which could be related to hypertrophic cardiomyopathy.
The patient developed recurrent sustained polymorphic ventricular tachycardia, indicating ventricular tachycardia.
The patient has stage 3 chronic kidney disease, which is a comorbidity that can affect cardiovascular health.
The patient has significant ostial right coronary artery stenosis and a history of percutaneous coronary interventions, indicating coronary artery disease.
The patient developed recurrent sustained polymorphic ventricular tachycardia and ventricular fibrillation, indicating cardiac arrhythmia.
The patient has a history of non-ST-elevation myocardial infarction and presents with ST-segment elevation in leads V1–V3, indicating myocardial infarction.
The patient has a reduced left ventricular ejection fraction and new QTc prolongation, which could be related to cardiomyopathy.
It explains the uncovered finding of subocclusion of the right coronary postero-lateral branch.
